SOURCE-ONLY REVIEW PACK · PROTOCOL 1

Review the evidence first.

MedDelta temporal dataset v1 · 32 fictional packets · 29 October 2026

Pharmacist review is pending.

These developer-authored examples are software research material, not patient records or treatment guidance. All medicine names are fictional. Judge what the documents support, not whether treatment is suitable.

How to review

  1. Read the rubric below. Start with the eight practice packets to clarify definitions.
  2. For each evaluation packet, choose one label, cite source lines or document dates, and explain your reasoning and uncertainty.
  3. Complete evaluation judgments before viewing MedDelta predictions, developer reference labels, or prior reviews.
  4. Export your review JSON from the lab. You can reopen it to resume. Browser work disappears on reload.
  5. After completing the evaluation set, compare predictions and record disagreements. Changes made after exposure must remain distinguishable from the initial judgments.

Document dates order evidence. A later explicit change does not automatically resolve an earlier unexplained discrepancy. Missing mention never implies a stop. An explicit stop is a documentary finding, not a treatment recommendation. Line 0 refers to the document date.

Names, reviewer roles, and timestamps are self-entered or browser-generated. This workflow does not authenticate clinicians or prevent prior exposure outside the app.

Download printable review pack PDF ↓

Use your browser's Print command for a paper copy. Download blank review CSV ↓ (for manual use; the app reopens its own JSON exports).

Label rubric

LabelMeaning
Matching instructionsWritten amounts (including equivalent SI units), route, and frequency agree where mentioned.
Documented changeAn explicit change or restart explains the transition, without an earlier unresolved discrepancy.
Unexplained discrepancyInstructions disagree without an adequate explanation, or disagree on the same date with unknown order.
Missing from latest recordThe medicine is omitted from a latest record without an applicable explicit stop. Omission is not discontinuation.
Explicit stop documentedThe latest target-specific instruction is an explicit stop, with no later restart or unresolved discrepancy.
First documentedFirst mention in the supplied records; actual treatment start date is unknown.
Insufficient evidenceDates, missing fields, or ambiguous/conditional instructions prevent a supported judgment. Clear wording is not unresolved just because software cannot parse it.
